claims.text: Intraclass correlation coefficients for nutrient intakes assessed by questionnaires one year apart ranged from 0.47 for vitamin E without supplements to 0.80 for vitamin C with supplements.

Correlation coefficients between energy-adjusted nutrient intakes measured by diet records and the second questionnaire ranged from 0.28 for iron without supplements to 0.86 for vitamin C with supplements, with a mean r of 0.59.
Adjusting for week-to-week variation in diet record intakes increased the mean correlation coefficient between energy-adjusted nutrient intakes from diet records and the questionnaire to r = 0.65.
The expanded 131-item semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire is reproducible over a one-year period.
The expanded 131-item semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire provides a useful measure of intake for many nutrients over a one-year period.

methodologies.name: Semiquantitative Food Frequency Questionnaire Validation
methodologies.description: Assessment of reproducibility and validity of a mail-administered 131-item semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire administered twice at a one-year interval against two one-week diet records spaced six months apart.
datasets: 127 male health professional participants from a prospective study of 51,529 men
conditions: Questionnaire administered by mail twice at a 1-year interval
Two 1-week diet records completed ~6 months apart
